lines: A module is delivered more than once inside a single page:
settings-BC1SRHu-: 28,004 B beyond the first copy, dompurify 20,950 B, @floating-ui/core 5,600 B, @floating-ui/utils 1,454 B.
app-BhsvYH7k: 28,642 B beyond the first copy, dompurify 20,950 B, @floating-ui/core 5,600 B, @floating-ui/utils 1,454 B.
All 2 pages load the same 6 files: 455,046 B raw, 151,655 B gzip, 98.8 % of the smallest page (app-BhsvYH7k, 460,381 B).
Files: js/nextcloud-vue-CAFOrlyV.mjs 249,058 B, js/floating-vue-CmP73hwC.mjs 120,713 B, js/nextcloud-common-DFiX4xE_.mjs 79,395 B, js/vue-material-design-icons-CCU3_1wb.mjs 4,887 B, and 2 more.
Inside: @nextcloud/vue 134,127 B, @vue/runtime-core 43,798 B, dompurify 42,129 B, axios 35,928 B, floating-vue 28,836 B.
1 delivered file carries no source map, so their bytes are charged only where the code shows its origin by itself: the glue of the bundler, code of the bundler and its plugins.
9 B in 1 piece of 1 file have no owner: no mapping covers them, and the code matches no file of a neighbouring module, of the app, or of the bundler and its plugins.
No package is imported as a whole: every package contributes only the modules that are used (32 packages, 156 modules).
On this measure the form of importing is exhausted. A root import whose barrel the bundler removes completely leaves no trace, so this is evidence, not proof.
No bundler chunk in dist is left without something that loads it.
